steps.question: Which GO biological process terms are over-represented among genes significant in the AD lesional vs control DESeq2 contrast in de_results.csv, using the 12000 tested genes as the background universe?

grounding.reason: GO over-representation of a discrete list per R-0095@492a: enrichGO with tested-genes-as-universe (R-0046@a0ac), size window 15-500 (R-0047@fd9d), rrvgo redundancy reduction (R-0052@620a); Entrez mapping via org.Hs.eg.db with unmapped-share reporting (R-0101@06c8); fallback to ranked test if <50 significant genes (R-0103@93aa); direction handled as separate up/down lists (R-0109@fe3e); input is a delivered results table so contrast/reference level/tie rule stated explicitly (R-0110@41cb); Reactome and WikiPathways added as secondary collections after the GO/Hallmark-style primary test (R-0098@d01b, R-0165@e456); Wald statistic used for the fgsea fallback ranking (R-0099@0e8a).

steps.description: From de_results.csv, define the significant gene set using padj < 0.05 (state this threshold and the log2_fold_change sign convention/reference level exactly as recorded in the table's contrast). Split into up-regulated and down-regulated lists (direction is biologically meaningful and must not be pooled without justification). Map gene symbols to Entrez IDs with org.Hs.eg.db (org.Hs.eg.db 3.23.1), reporting the fraction of genes that fail to map or map ambiguously. Run clusterProfiler::enrichGO (ont='BP') separately for the up and down lists, with the universe set to all 12000 genes present in de_results.csv (not the whole genome), gene set size window 15-500 members, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR. Reduce the significant GO BP terms with rrvgo (semantic similarity) to non-redundant representative terms, keeping the full enrichGO table as a supplement. If fewer than ~50 genes pass the significance threshold in either direction, state this explicitly and additionally run a preranked GSEA (fgsea) against the same GO BP gene sets using the DESeq2 Wald statistic ('stat' column, if present in de_results.csv; otherwise signed -log10(p) with the tie rule stated) as the ranking metric, since a hypergeometric test on a short list has little power. As secondary collections for corroboration, repeat the enrichGO/fgsea logic against the Reactome and WikiPathways human gene sets from the reference store, reporting each collection's version separately (do not merge sets across collections).
acceptance_criteria: Significant gene list size stated for each direction, with the padj/log2FC thresholds used named explicitly
Universe = all tested genes in de_results.csv (12000), stated in the output
Unmapped/ambiguous symbol-to-Entrez fraction reported
enrichGO run with ont=BP, size window 15-500, BH-adjusted; full table plus rrvgo-reduced representative terms both saved
If significant list <50 genes in a direction, fgsea preranked result also produced and reported alongside, with the ranking metric and tie-handling rule stated
Reactome and WikiPathways results reported separately from GO BP with each collection's version/release named

plan.title: AD lesional vs control GO BP over-representation
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question asks specifically which GO biological processes are over-represented among the significant genes from the delivered DESeq2 treated-vs-control (AD lesional vs control) results table (12000 genes tested, 6 vs 6, unpaired, single batch). This is an ORA-on-a-results-table question, not a fresh DE fit — the DESeq2 output already exists. The plan therefore: (1) inherits/re-checks sample structure QC from the delivered counts.csv rather than re-fitting DESeq2, since sample_01 has a library size ~4x below median and this must be reported (not silently used or silently dropped) before the downstream ORA is interpreted; (2) defines the significant gene list from de_results.csv (padj/log2FoldChange threshold, split up- vs down-regulated to preserve direction), maps symbols to Entrez via org.Hs.eg.db, and runs clusterProfiler::enrichGO (ontology=BP) with the universe set to all 12000 tested genes, gene-set size window 15-500; (3) reduces redundant GO BP terms with rrvgo by semantic similarity; (4) if the significant list is short (<~50 genes per the knowledge-service rule), falls back to / supplements with fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against the same GO BP term list so a coordinated-but-subtle signal is not missed; (5) produces a report stating the collection version, the universe, the direction-handling convention, and the reproducibility record. WikiPathways and Reactome GMTs are available in the reference store and are added as secondary collections per the knowledge-service recommendation, since the user's core ask is GO BP but corroboration across curated pathway databases strengthens the interpretation of any hits and costs one additional lightweight step.

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
